messages:
Maya: quick follow-up from today's infra all-hands re: GPU supply and autoscale. two short asks: how are we prioritizing reserved capacity vs spot/opportunistic in APAC, and what's the plan if spot evaporates during peak?
Jorge: good q. short answer: reserved capacity = strategic enterprise regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 for now). APAC opportunistic pools include ap-east-1 + pooled partner zones.
Aisha: when you say "partner zones" do you mean cloud marketplace partners or coloc partners? customers ask about data residency.
Jorge: mostly cloud marketplace partners initially. for colo/partner racks we'll surface metadata in the console for residency tag.
Liam: technical detail: autoscaler fallback order is currently: reserved -> opportunistic -> shared -> degrade-to-quantized. we try to avoid hard rejects.
Maya: thanks. is degrade-to-quantized automatic or opt-in per-customer?
Jorge: opt-in flag per model route. default = allow degrade for non-enterprise accounts. enterprise can request opt-out.
Priya: action item: SEs requested a succinct matrix to show expected latencies per tier (reserved/opportunistic/shared). can we get p50/p95 numbers?
Aisha: we have p50/p95 for reserved already. opportunistic p95 varies by 20-40% depending on spot churn; I'll pull last 30d numbers.
deploy-bot: canary scheduled: autoscaler-rollout/2026-03-30T02:00Z -> target ap-east-1 opportunistic pool.
Liam: note: operator checklist for canary includes rollback window and cache-warmup step. include KV cache warming in runbook.
Maya: billing question from leadership: do we apply surge surcharge during opportunistic bursts or is that only on reserved bursts?
Jorge: current plan: surge surcharge applies to opportunistic bursts > baseline usage; reserved bursts billed as normal committed capacity. docs team will add examples.
Priya: follow-ups: 1) can we get a short blurb for customers about expected notice for migrating reserved capacity? 2) any timeline for console UI to pin region preferences?
Jorge: 1) 30 days notice for reserved pool migrations, transfer credits policy included. 2) console region pinning beta in 3 sprints; aiming for opt-in toggles in 6 weeks.
Aisha: ops ask: if spot evaporates mid-request, do we retry in another pool or stream an error? need to know for client SDK behavior.
Liam: runtime retries across pools by default with circuit-breaker backoff. if request already streaming, we try transparent failover to alternate pool, else raise retriable error.
Maya: perfect. last one: will we expose per-pool SLOs in docs so customers can make routing decisions?
Jorge: yes, per-pool p95/p99 and missed_tokens/sec will be published in the infra status page and API.
Priya: I'll collect these notes and draft the customer-facing FAQ. assigning @Aisha to pull opportunistic latency numbers and @Liam to add KV cache warmup to the checklist.
Aisha: on it, will post numbers by EOD tomorrow.
Liam: will update runbook and link it here after canary readiness review.
Maya: thanks everyone. closing thread 0:00 1:00.
